name: sort3
description: Three-way sorting demo: teddy bears, bottles, everything else — each with a grip material.
_comment_groups: Every prompt belongs to exactly one group. The classifier stage reports the group, so the
sorting mission picks a bin from `group` and never has to know the vocabulary.
`teddy_bear` and `bottle` are the two named bins; `other` is the third bin and also the
fallback for anything the segmenter found that no prompt claims.
`ignore` exists so the model has somewhere correct to put people, the robot and the
furniture. Those objects are dropped before replying — without them the argmax has to land
on *some* label, and a bystander's foot comes back as a pickable 'shoe'.
Cans and cartons are deliberately in `other`: the demo's second bin is bottles, and a can
that lands there reads as a mistake to an audience.
_comment_materials: Grip material, three levels, and what it decides is how hard the gripper squeezes once
the object is held — not what the object is made of in a physics sense. So an egg and a
light bulb are `soft`: rigid, but they must be held gently. `hard` is for things that are
both rigid and robust. Anything unlisted takes its group's default.
